subject: Human Body
title: Skin: The Living Barrier
description: Learn Skin: The Living Barrier in one minute.

hook.text: Your skin blocks millions of bacteria every second. It's the largest organ and your first immune shield.

buildup.text: Dead skin cells form a tough outer layer. They fall off constantly, taking hitchhiking microbes with them.

discovery.text: Skin also secretes antimicrobial peptides and acidic sweat. Its surface pH of 4.5–5.5 is hostile to many bacteria.

twist.text: A single cut bypasses this entire defense. That's why even small wounds can get infected quickly.

climax.text: Skin isn't passive armor. It's an active chemical barrier that kills, sheds, and repels invaders constantly.

punchline.text: Your skin fights germs before your immune cells ever see them.

quiz.question: How does skin actively fight bacteria?
options: By absorbing bacteria into fat cells
By secreting antimicrobial peptides and acidic sweat
By heating up to kill surface germs
